title: Apple-Braised Sweet Potato Coins
description: Sweet potato coins and grated apple braise together until the fruit melts into a lightly spiced cider glaze.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: Peeled weight, cut in 1/4-inch coins or half-moons.

ingredients.name: small sweet apple
ingredients.note: Peeled and cored weight, finely grated with the juices retained.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.text: Spread {apple} in the skillet and stir in {cider}, {water} and {coriander}.

steps.title: Arrange the coins
steps.text: Nestle {potato} in overlapping rows in the apple mixture and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.

steps.title: Cook until tender
steps.text: Cover and braise over medium-low heat for 15–20 minutes, gently turning the slices halfway through, until a fork slips through without breaking them.

steps.title: Reduce the glaze
steps.text: Lift the coins onto a warm plate and simmer the apple juices uncovered for 2–4 minutes until thick enough to leave a trail behind a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the apples
steps.text: Take the skillet off the heat and swirl {butter} into the reduced fruit.

steps.title: Dress the coins
steps.text: Return the sweet potatoes to the skillet and tilt it to coat the coins with the apple glaze.

notes: Make ahead: Peel and slice the sweet potatoes up to a day ahead and chill submerged in water. Drain well before braising. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the tender coins in a single layer with their glaze for up to 1 month. They will be a little softer after thawing. Fridge reheat: Warm covered with a splash of water over medium-low heat for 5–8 minutes until the center of the thickest slice reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge reheat instructions. For dairy-free glaze, use avocado oil in place of butter. Option A uses cider. For gentler Option B, replace the cider with water and keep the grated apple. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 191 kcal, 2.5 g protein, 37.6 g total carbohydrate, 4.1 g fat, 5.0 g fiber, 81 mg sodium.
